raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #65531. With `enable_mm_embeds=True` and `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`, one request with precomputed image or video embeddings crashes the engine. This PR sends embeddings batches to the eager path in both model runners.

## Claims

- Precomputed image and video embeddings no longer crash the engine when the encoder CUDA graph is on. This holds in Model Runner V1 and V2.
- Pixel inputs still replay the graph.
- Nothing changes for batches without a `<modality>_embeds` key.

## Validation

Setup: one NVIDIA H100 (80 GB), torch 2.14.0+cu130, main at `f9db1756e`.

These results are from `f9db1756e`. The branch is rebased onto `34d5de18c` with no conflicts. There, the CPU unit tests give 86 passed and 25 skipped. One test, `test_encoder_timing_stats_registry`, fails on CPU because it needs a GPU. It fails the same way on main without this PR.

**Before the fix.** With the fix reverted, the new GPU test (command below) fails in both cases. Each one dies at the image embeddings request, so the video embeddings request never runs:

```text
  File "vllm/v1/worker/encoder_cudagraph.py", line 732, in execute
  ...
  File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_vl.py", line 1658, in select_encoder_cudagraph_items
    pixel_values = self._get_pixel_values_by_modality(mm_kwargs)
  File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2_vl.py", line 1626, in _get_pixel_values_by_modality
    pixel_values = mm_kwargs["pixel_values"]
KeyError: 'pixel_values'
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause.
...
FAILED tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_vl.py::test_qwen2_vl_embeddings_input_with_encoder_cudagraph[v1-Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct]
FAILED tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_vl.py::test_qwen2_vl_embeddings_input_with_encoder_cudagraph[v2-Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct]
================== 2 failed, 4 warnings in 240.72s (0:04:00) ===================
```

The video case is never reached here. The CPU check in #65531 shows that video embeddings fail too, for Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and MiniCPM-V.

With the fix reverted, the issue's InternVL3-1B script dies with the default V2 runner. It fails in `sanity_check_mm_encoder_outputs` with `got len(mm_embeddings)=0`.

**After the fix.**

- `test_qwen2_vl_embeddings_input_with_encoder_cudagraph[v1|v2]` passes in both runners: `2 passed, 4 warnings in 48.32s`. It runs one image and one 4-frame video. Each goes in first as pixels, then as embeddings from the model's own vision tower. The outputs agree under `check_logprobs_close`. The graph hit count goes up over the two pixel requests. It stays the same over the two embeddings requests.
- The issue's InternVL3-1B script no longer crashes. With V2 it prints "The image appears to be a screenshot from". With V1 it prints "The image appears to be a screenshot of". Its embeddings are random, so the text itself means nothing.
- Mutation check. Each broken fix makes at least one test fail. The first uses the GPU test. The other three use `TestSupportsBatch`:
  - fixing only the V2 runner: the `v1` case fails (`1 failed, 1 passed, 4 warnings in 47.52s`);
  - checking only `"image_embeds"`: the two `video_embeds` rows fail;
  - checking for pixel key names instead: the InternVL `pixel_values_flat` and Phi-4MM `input_image_embeds` rows fail;
  - checking any key that ends in `_embeds`: the `input_image_embeds` row fails. That key is Phi-4MM's pixel input.
- No regressions:
  - `pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_vl.py -m core_model`: `5 passed, 7 warnings in 134.22s`, with the 2 new cases;
  - `pytest -v -s tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_vit_cudagraph.py -m core_model -k "qwen2_vl or internvl"`: `4 passed, 38 deselected, 6 warnings in 115.24s`;
  - `pytest -v -s tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py`: `103 passed, 2 warnings in 39.57s`.
- No accuracy eval. Only batches with a `<modality>_embeds` key change path. They now take the same eager `embed_multimodal` call as with the graph off.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
# New GPU test (CI runs this file with -m core_model)
pytest -v -s "tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_vl.py::test_qwen2_vl_embeddings_input_with_encoder_cudagraph"

# CPU unit tests
pytest -v -s tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k TestSupportsBatch
pytest -v -s tests/v1/worker/test_encoder_runner.py -k unsupported_modality

# The issue's script, with each runner
python embeds_repro.py
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 python embeds_repro.py
```

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** Both runners pick the encoder graph by modality only. An embeddings item keeps its modality, `"image"` or `"video"`, so it reaches the graph manager. The model's graph hooks then look for pixel inputs and fail. #65531 shows how each model fails.
- **The fix.** `EncoderCudaGraphManager.supports_batch(modality, mm_kwargs)` returns `False` when the batch has the `<modality>_embeds` key. Both runners call it where they called `supports_modality`. The check runs before `execute()`, so embeddings never reach the data-parallel encoder path either. `group_and_batch_mm_kwargs` never puts pixel and embeddings items in one batch. So in a step with both, the pixel batch still replays the graph.
- **Why this key.** Embedding inputs reach the runner as `<modality>_embeds` (`multimodal/parse.py:244`). Models that take embeddings as a dict use the same names. The check matches the exact key, not a suffix. So a pixel input whose key ends in `_embeds`, such as Phi-4MM's `input_image_embeds`, is not taken for embeddings. Phi-4MM has no encoder graph today.
- **Why not inside `execute()`.** Returning `[]` there still fails the sanity check. Returning `None` would also work, because both runners already fall back to eager on `None`. But it widens `execute()`'s return type for a case the runners can check up front. I'm happy to switch if you prefer.
- **Why V1 too.** V1 is still used when V2 lacks a feature. `XPUModelRunner` also subclasses it.
- **Overlap with #58122.** #58122 is the LLaVA encoder graph PR. It adds `"image_embeds" not in mm_kwargs_batch` to the same two runner lines. This PR moves that check into the manager and also covers `video_embeds`. Whichever PR lands second gets a one-line conflict in each runner. The fix is to keep `supports_batch()` and drop the inline check. A local trial merge shows this works. With that fix, the merged `test_encoder_runner.py` passes. #59193 (BLIP-2) relies on #58122's check. `supports_batch()` covers it too.
- **Limits.**
  - On EC and KV consumers, a request may send only `image_grid_thw` and no embedding tensor. Such an item has no `image_embeds` key. So if it were encoded locally, it would still reach the graph. But the eager path would fail on it too, before and after this PR. So this PR doesn't change that case.
  - The new GPU test skips unless the platform is CUDA or ROCm, like `test_vit_cudagraph.py`. It still runs on the AMD mirrors. It was tested on NVIDIA only.
- **Not a duplicate.** No open PR fixes this for both image and video embeddings. #58122 covers `image_embeds` only, inside a LLaVA feature PR. #56277 (Pixtral and Mistral 3, merged on 2026-11-03) avoids the crash inside the model. It turns the encoder graph off whenever `enable_mm_embeds` is on. The open PR #52229 (Cosmos3-Edge) does the same. With `supports_batch()`, those models could keep the graph for pixel inputs.

I used Claude Code to trace the code and to write the fix, the tests and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran all the tests above myself.

---
